newsitem.title: USA: PointCast looks for CEO, IPO seen soon.
newsitem.headline: PointCast looks for CEO, IPO seen soon.

text.p: PointCast Inc., the privately-held company that pioneered "push" technology on the Internet, will announce Monday it has begun a search for a chief executive, a move that industry executives said is a precursor to an initial public offering.

PointCast will hold a conference call Monday to announce its CEO search and to unveil the next version of its news and information service for the Internet. The beta, or test, version of its PointCast 2.0 software will be available free beginning Monday as a download at PointCast's Web site.
Chris Hassett, PointCast's current president and CEO, will remain with the company as chairman, and focus on the company's vision, while the CEO focuses on the day-to-day operations, PointCast said.

"Everyone is in agreement that he has done a fantastic job of taking us where we are today," said Jaleh Bisharat, senior vice president of marketing. "Chris is actively involved in the recruitment process."

PointCast, based in Cupertino, Calif., has hired David Bierne, a leading industry headhunter who recruited Jim Barksdale as CEO of Netscape Communications Corp., to conduct the search. Bisharat said that Bierne has already had interest from executives he did not believe would consider leaving their current jobs, but she declined to be more specific.

Last week, PointCast hired Phil Koen, formerly chief financial officer of Etec Systems Inc. as senior vice president of finance and chief financial officer. Koen led Etec, a semiconductor equipment company, through its initial public offering and two additional stock offerings.

"The hope is that at some point, if and when it makes sense, to get some liquidity through an offering," Koen said. "That's one of the attractions. But candidly as we sit here today, there aren't any plans to do that."

"It sounds like they are getting ready for their IPO," said Steve Harmon, a senior investment analyst of Meckler Media's Internet Stock Report. "It's a good time because Internet stocks are coming back."
After the window for technology IPOs closed last year, a recent batch of stock offerings in the Internet sector have lead some companies to begin looking at the public markets again for funding.

Amazon.com, the leading bookseller on the Internet, recently went public, although its shares traded below their offering price. @Home, the high-speed cable modem Internet access service recently filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange and PeaPod, the online grocery shopping company, is also looking at going public.

In March, PointCast is said to have talked with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. about a merger, but the two could not come to terms on price. Hassett said at the time that PointCast's intent was to remain independent and that an initial public offering was definitely a possibilty in the near future.
Another industry executive said that there have been rumours in the past few weeks that PointCast is about to go public soon.

PointCast, founded in 1992, pioneered the concept of Internet direct broadcasting technology, that "pushes" requested news and information to a desktop PC, via the Internet. It also has developed software for corporate intranets. It has many media giants as partners, including Times Mirror Co., the New York Times, Reuters Holdings Plc, and others.

However the market for companies developing push technology is going through a shakeout, with the Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing of IFusion and the shut down last week of Individual Inc.'s Freeloader service.
PointCast estimates that is has over one million active users of its service, which is free. It generates revenues from advertising sales.
